newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand mulls tax exemption for shipping sector.
newsitem.headline: Thailand mulls tax exemption for shipping sector.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday he would seek approval from the country's cabinet to exempt the domestic shipping industry from corporate tax.
The move was aimed at promoting Thailand's commercial fleet and reducing the country's dependence on foreign shipping, thereby lowering the national current account deficit, he said.
"The exemption from corporate tax on (the) commercial fleet should be an appropriate measure, but it has to be approved by the cabinet first," Amnuay told reporters.

Although export revenues have been Thailand's major growth engine for many years, the Thai domestic merchant fleet has been relatively underdeveloped and has missed opportunities to tap into the export business.

Freight charges alone paid by Thai exporters to foreign shippers to move their goods to overseas markets in 1995 totalled nearly 20 billion baht ($769 million) or seven percent of the country's total payments for services.
This has put pressure on the current account deficit which stood at 8.0 percent of gross domestic product in 1996.
Recently, the Thai government has introduced several other measures to boost the shipping industry.

These included an import tariff exemption for purchases of ships larger than 1,000 gross tonnes, income tax reduction on revenue from ship chartering and tax exemption on revenue from ship sales if proceeds were used to buy new ships.
The Bank of Thailand also set up an eight-billion baht fund to provide soft loans to the maritime sector.
